report: [DATE]: MR Knie Rechts 15ch AA: Klinische inlichtingen: Zie gescande aanvraag Diagnostische vraagstelling: Zie gescande aanvraag Bevindingen: Focaal gevorderde femoropatellaire kraakbeenlijden graad 4 op de bovenste 3e van de crista patellaris, op de diepe fissuren en erosies met enkele kleine subchondrale geode's en minimaal omliggend botoedeem. Licht toegenomen gewrichtsvocht. Kruisbanden en laterale banden intact. Degeneratief voorkomen mediale meniscus met onregelmatig voorkomen ondervlakte van het corpus, mogelijks met kleine scheur. Beginnend mediaal femorotibiaal kraakbeenlijden graad 2 met enkele zeldzame oppervlakkige fissuren. Popliteale cyste met craniocaudale as 5\~cm. Uitgebreide varices van de vena saphena parva, zonder trombose. Besluit: - Lokaal gevorderd femoropatellair kraakbeenlijden graad 4, op heden met licht toegenomen gewrichtsvocht . - Beginnend mediaal femorotibiaal kraakbeenlijden graad 2 met licht degeneratief voorkomen mediale menisc us. - Zeer uitgebreide varices posterieur op de vena saphena parva .

COMPARISON:None.

CLINICAL HISTORY:Anterior right knee pain with locking sensation. Suspected patellofemoral pain syndrome.

PROCEDURE:Multisequence, multiplanar unenhanced MRI of the right knee according to routine protocol.

IMAGING FINDINGS:

Nondiagnostic scout localizing images reviewed.

Through the medial meniscus is intact. The lateral meniscus is intact.

Intact anterior cruciate ligament and posterior cruciate ligament.

The medial collateral ligament, posterior oblique ligament, fibular collateral ligament, popliteus and biceps femoris tendon attachments, as well as iliotibial band are intact.

The patellar retinacula are intact. No femoral trochlear dysplasia. The TT-TG distance measures 9 mm, within normal limits. The quadriceps and patellar tendons are intact.

Trace knee joint fluid. Regional musculature is within normal limits. No suspicious focal marrow signal alteration.

Scattered foci of mild chondrosis throughout the patellofemoral compartment. Preserved medial and lateral femorotibial articular cartilage. 

IMPRESSION:
1. No evidence of meniscal, ligament, or tendon tear.
2. Mild patellofemoral chondrosis.

PROCEDURE:Multisequence multiplanar unenhanced MRI of the left knee according to routine protocol.

IMAGING FINDINGS:

Nondiagnostic scout localizing images reviewed.

The medial meniscus is intact. The lateral meniscus is intact.

Intact anterior cruciate ligament and posterior cruciate ligament.

The medial collateral ligament, posterior oblique ligament, fibular collateral ligament, popliteus and biceps femoris tendon attachments, as well as iliotibial band are intact.

The patellar retinacula are intact. No patellofemoral subluxation. No femoral trochlear dysplasia. The TT-TG distance measures 8 mm, within normal limits. The quadriceps and patellar tendons are intact.

Scattered foci of mild chondrosis throughout the patellofemoral compartment. There is focal mild to moderate chondrosis involving the weightbearing aspect of the lateral femorotibial compartment. Preserved medial femorotibial articular cartilage.

Small knee joint effusion. Baker's cyst, measuring 31 x 22 x 50 mm. Trace fluid outlines the superficial fascia of the distal fibers of the mid epigastrium is muscle, suggesting partial cyst leakage.

Regional musculature is within normal limits. No suspicious focal marrow signal alteration.

IMPRESSION:
1. No evidence of discrete meniscal, ligament, or tendon tear.
2. Subtle patellofemoral and lateral femorotibial chondrosis as detailed above.
3. Partially leaking 31 x 22 x 50 mm Baker's cyst.

Medyal menisküs arka boynuz-gövdesi bileşkesindeki dejeneratif yapı içi intensite artışına yırtık eşlik etmiyor. Lateral menisküs normal. Kuadriseps yağ yastığındaki minimal ödem ön diz ağrısı nedeni olabilir. Femoral troklea hafif dereceli displastik (De Jour tip A). Patella hafifçe laterale translasyon gösteriyor. Exam Type: MRI KNEE LEFT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: One-year history of pain at the inner aspect without injury.
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla extremity system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions. There is a 11 x 8 x 11 mm lobulated T2 hyperintense low-grade chondroid lesion within the distal femur without aggressive features.

JOINT SPACE:
Moderate joint effusion with mild synovial proliferation. No intra-articular bodies. No Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Medial compartment cartilage: Full thickness fissuring of the medial tibial plateau with associated subchondral cystic change/edema. Medial femoral condyle cartilage is intact.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Partial thickness fissuring along the lateral patellar facet. The trochlear cartilage is intact.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 16 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:

1.	Moderate joint effusion out of proportion to intra-articular findings. Consider fluid sampling if there is concern for inflammatory arthropathy or infection.
2.	MIld medial and patellofemoral compartment chondrosis.

Findings:  There is a mild knee effusion. Normal appearances of the medial and lateral menisci. No evidence of tears.  Normal ACL, PCL, MCL and LCL. Normal extensor mechanism.  There is mild fraying of the medial compartment articular cartilage. 
The lateral compartment articular cartilage is preserved. Moderate articular cartilage thinning and areas of cartilage loss are seen in the patella with underlying bony change. The trochlear articular cartilage is preserved.  
Conclusion: No meniscal tear. Mild medial compartment degeneration. Moderate patellar articular cartilage degeneration.
